clue.text: Shine as point in county side

indicators.note: in tells us the compass point is placed inside the letters for the county side

parts.note: Glam is the short name for Glamorgan, the Welsh county and its county cricket team
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone describing a star player who shines for his county team.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAM is Glamorgan, a Welsh county with a first-class cricket team; 'in' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash of light, so to shine and to gleam are synonyms.

clue.text: French gendarmes both fail to end the scene of fighting

indicators.note: both words lose their endings, so the closing letters of each are dropped

parts.note: Gallic means French
gendarmes are French police

explanation.surface: French police both failing to stop a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both fail to end' cuts GALLIC to GALLI and POLICE to POLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the site of the 1915-16 First World War campaign in Turkey.

clue.text: Military standard flying from 22 dn

explanation.surface: A regimental banner fluttering from a high nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is EYRIE, the eagle's nest; Roman legions carried an eagle as their standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman legions carried a bird of prey emblem as their standard, and that bird nests and flies from a mountain nest.

clue.text: Grind up one's cat meat for cooking

indicators.note: cooking implies preparing and mixing, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, and 's is s, giving IS

explanation.surface: An instruction to mince someone's cat food before cooking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' mixes IS (one's) with CATMEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To masticate is to chew food, grinding it with the teeth.

clue.text: Raising the view of one side

explanation.surface: An architect lifting a building while drawing one face of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting something up is its elevation; an architect's elevation is a drawing of one face of a building.

clue.text: Authorised third man, say, .to come inside the boundary

indicators.note: to come inside tells us the man is put within the boundary word

parts.note: an end is a boundary or limit

indicators.note: say tells us the name is to be heard, giving a word spoken just like it

parts.note: Abel, son of Adam and Eve, was the third man in the Bible's story

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at third man being allowed to come inside the boundary rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position near the boundary, which makes the surface; the solver needs the Bible's Abel, the third human after Adam and Eve, and 'say' signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable someone is to empower or permit them, so enabled can mean authorised.

clue.text: Inspect the inlet for rubbish

parts.note: to eye something is to inspect it
the Wash is a large inlet on the east coast of England

explanation.surface: Someone told to examine a creek for litter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large square bay on England's east coast between Lincolnshire and Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or humbug, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Cold dessert served up after a starter

indicators.note: starter says the letter a is served first, ahead of the turned dessert, as the opening course
served up in a down clue means the dessert is written upwards so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a fool is a fruit and cream dessert

explanation.surface: A chilled pudding brought out after the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOOL is a dessert of fruit puree and cream; 'served up' turns it to LOOF beneath A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is distant and unfriendly, a cold manner.

clue.text: It's chill on this Roman island for a game

parts.note: ice gives a chill
hoc is Latin for this
a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: A chilly Roman island playing host to a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: HOC is Latin for 'this'; a KEY or cay is a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice hockey is a team sport played with sticks and a puck on a rink.

clue.text: Nobody's without love at this time

indicators.note: without means the zero letter is taken away

parts.note: nobody is no one, so nobody's is no one's
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lonely remark that nobody is without love these days.
explanation.walkthrough: NO ONE'S loses an O (love, zero in tennis scoring).
explanation.definitionFit: Nones is a fixed hour of the day for prayer, the ninth hour after dawn, and a date in the Roman calendar.

clue.text: Cricket side is behind the clock — make a ruling

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field
taken as written
running behind the clock means being late

explanation.surface: An umpire with a cricket team running late having to decide something.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG (the leg side, also called on side, in cricket), then IS, then LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, a formal kind of ruling.

clue.text: "---'s nursling, Venice" (Shelley)

parts.note: a quotation with a gap: Shelley's line calls Venice the nursling of the sea that bore her, and the missing word fills that gap

explanation.surface: A line of Romantic poetry about Venice with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Shelley's Lines written among the Euganean Hills, where Venice is the nursling of the sea around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice rose from the sea, so Shelley pictures it as a child nursed by that great body of water.

clue.text: Ancient Britons who discovered diamonds and nickel

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: An archaeological story about an early British tribe finding precious stones and metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were the tribe of Boudicca in eastern England; 'who discovered' only links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic tribe of East Anglia, the people Boudicca led against Rome.

clue.text: Advances by stages, keeping the amphibian within bounds

indicators.note: within puts the amphibian inside the word meaning bounds

parts.note: bounds and leaps are both jumps
a frog is an amphibian

explanation.surface: A naturalist hopping along a path while carrying a frog, keeping it from escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advances by stages' looks like wordplay but is the definition; 'keeping the' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To leapfrog is to jump ahead one step at a time, overtaking in turns.

clue.text: It's bound to give youth adventure training, that's apparent

definitions.text: It's bound to give youth adventure training

explanation.surface: A promotional line for a youth outdoor training scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Outward Bound is a British charity running outdoor adventure courses for young people; the first half points to the word that precedes 'bound'.
explanation.definitionFit: The charity's name begins with this word, and something on the surface rather than within is plainly visible.

clue.text: Examine treatise on litmus, for instance

parts.note: to test is to examine
a paper is a learned essay or treatise

explanation.surface: A scientist studying an essay on litmus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links the pieces; litmus paper is the classic chemistry indicator strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus is a strip of treated paper used in chemistry to show acidity, an example of a test strip.

clue.text: Marker's in the list as an aircraft designer

indicators.note: in, after Marker's read as marker is, puts the writing fluid inside the lean

parts.note: a ship's list is a lean to one side, also called a heel
ink is what a marker writes with; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone checking that a marker pen is on a list of an aircraft maker's supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marker's in' reads as 'marker is in'; a ship's list is the same as its heel, a nautical lean to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst Heinkel was the German engineer whose firm designed aircraft such as the He 111 bomber.

clue.text: Simplicity the court assumes initially

explanation.surface: A remark about a court's simple starting assumption.
explanation.walkthrough: Courts presume the defendant not guilty until proved otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple artlessness is guilelessness, and a court starts by presuming the accused guiltless.

clue.text: Blockage caused by house attendants at opening of theatre

parts.note: a lodge is a small house
attendants can be men in service

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of theatre

explanation.surface: A crush at a theatre door caused by house staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' takes T from theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodgement is something lodged or stuck, an obstruction.

clue.text: Edits an unorthodox substitute

definitions.note: the adverb means as a substitute, so the noun stands in loosely for it

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the usual form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A copy editor's unconventional replacement for a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges the letters of EDITS AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in place of something else, that is, as an alternative or replacement.

clue.text: Course leading to a point in the Gobi, say

indicators.note: in puts the compass point inside the sandy region

parts.note: the Gobi is an example of a desert
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A route that leads to a spot in the Asian desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a route but is a meal course; S goes in DESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the sweet course at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Badgered girl to ring the old number

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
O is ring-shaped
ye is an old form of the
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A pestered girl being told to telephone an outdated number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a telephone call but is the letter O; D is 500 in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them until they are irritated.

clue.text: One who checks "The Listener'?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fact-checker works at a radio magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC magazine; auditor is Latin for hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: An accounts inspector, and literally (from Latin audire, to hear) a hearer.

clue.text: Low newshawks indeed

annotationWithheld.why: Low newshawks indeed (9): PRESS in DEED, read from the single word 'indeed' as 'in deed', so 'indeed' is both the container indicator and DEED's fodder, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Detectives turn up about gold order in…

indicators.note: about means the detectives go around the gold
turn up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detectives
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Detectives arriving to look into some gold, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses the detectives in a down clue, and 'about' wraps them round heraldic gold; the Doric order is a style of classical column.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture, with plain column capitals.

clue.text: … weird-sounding high place

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for weird is heard, not spelt

parts.note: eerie means weird or uncanny

explanation.surface: A strange-sounding lofty spot, continuing the detectives' tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 21 down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built on a crag, a lofty spot.

clue.text: Found English class

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: Someone who discovered an English school class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is not the past tense of find but the verb meaning to cast molten metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in Hindu society.

clue.text: River horse

explanation.surface: A horse by the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shire is a river in Malawi and Mozambique; a shire is also a heavy draught horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flowing from Lake Malawi, and a large breed of draught horse.

clue.text: Part of the Kalahari, perhaps, is more developed

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a region of the desert is more advanced than others.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in kalahaRI PERhaps. The draft took 'is' into the definition, but 'is more developed' cannot swap for an adjective, so 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or plans that are riper have matured further.

clue.text: Comprehensive covering a large area

explanation.surface: A description of a thorough survey spread over a wide territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wide-ranging is both thorough in scope and spread across much ground.

clue.text: A joiner for a wartime organisation in the middle of America

indicators.note: in places the wartime body inside the American word for middle

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre, the middle, as 'of America' signals
ARP, Air Raid Precautions, was the British civil defence service of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A craftsman recruited by a war effort based in the heartland of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of America' looks like a letter selection but is CENTER, the US spelling; ARP was Britain's wartime air-raid wardens' service.
explanation.definitionFit: A joiner is a woodworker, and so is a carpenter.

clue.text: Girl not disheartened in horse-riding contest

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so only the outer letters of not remain

explanation.surface: A girl who stays cheerful during a riding competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle O of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a competition in equestrianism, as in three-day eventing.
